quarterly_data.signal: CFO Hirooka: FY26 Q1 revenue was 255.7 billion yen, up 16% YoY (up 7% at constant currency); profit from ordinary operating activities was 82.4 billion yen, up 24% (17% at constant currency); pretax profit 86.0 billion yen, up 28%; both revenue and operating profit were quarterly records, led by Information Technology; HOYA early adopted IFRS 18 from Q1 and now defines segment profit as profit from ordinary operating activities
quarterly_data.figure: revenue 255.7 billion yen (+16%); operating profit 82.4 billion yen (+24%); pretax profit 86.0 billion yen (+28%)

quarterly_data.signal: CFO Hirooka: Information Technology Q1 revenue was 101.0 billion yen, up 23% YoY (15% at constant currency), with operating profit of 55.6 billion yen (+28%) and a 55.1% margin, on strong growth in LSI, glass substrates for HDDs and Optical Solutions; excluding U.S. tariff refunds the margin is in the 54% range; management views around 52% as a benchmark to exceed and at least 50% as an important objective, and CEO Ikeda sees the low 50% range as a realistic baseline, with depreciation rising significantly only from next fiscal year
quarterly_data.figure: Information Technology revenue 101.0 billion yen (+23%); operating profit 55.6 billion yen; margin 55.1% (54% range excluding tariff refunds)

quarterly_data.signal: CFO Hirooka: demand for EUV blanks remained extremely strong and sales of high-value-added products kept expanding, with DUV blanks growing in the mid-single digits; CEO Ikeda: EUV performance is stronger than previously discussed and HOYA expects EUV blanks to grow about 20% YoY, sustained through the second and third quarters and at least through the end of the calendar year (Q4 production schedules a possible variable), with DUV growing in the low- to mid-single digits; volume and price both contribute, and lower defect rates let HOYA raise average prices without sacrificing productivity
quarterly_data.figure: EUV blanks expected growth about 20% YoY; DUV low- to mid-single-digit growth

quarterly_data.signal: CEO Ikeda: significant volumes of phase shift mask (PSM) blanks are already used in the current N2 generation, and with foundry customers' N2 mass production in full swing this demand is driving current growth; in the A14 and A10 generations the PSM film materials need to change and the share of EUV layers in the mask set and of PSM layers within it are expected to increase, so value added will be higher than in N2; DUV growth reflects a mix shift toward mid-range and high-end products, without capacity investment

CEO Ikeda: HOYA expects 3.5-inch HDD glass platters to grow around 15-20% and 2.5-inch platters to decline by double digits, so the HDD business as a whole should grow in the low-teens range (CFO Hirooka: Q1 HDD growth reached 15% as the 2.5-inch decline was milder than anticipated); HAMR raises recording density, but at present density alone cannot absorb demand so platter counts are rising; second and third customers are expected to ramp up in the future; HOYA sees no supply constraints on its side for HDD platters and views HDD makers' consideration of in-house glass substrates as a shift from aluminum to glass and positive for the glass substrate market
quarterly_data.figure: 3.5-inch platters around 15-20% growth; HDD business low-teens growth

quarterly_data.signal: CEO Ikeda: the Laos HDD substrate plant has facilities for 12 production lines with a cleanroom but has operated only four lines (about one-third utilization); equipment for the remaining lines will be installed gradually from this fiscal year through next fiscal year, the next round of investment to increase production is scheduled to begin in FY28, and HOYA is accelerating new equipment installation and can fully handle 3.5-inch demand growth up to 20%
quarterly_data.figure: four of 12 production lines operating at the Laos plant

quarterly_data.signal: CEO Ikeda: Optical Solutions (renamed from Imaging) is now driven by CUPO for data centers and products for wearables, with digital camera demand relatively stable; CUPO sales alone are expected to grow approximately 30-40% YoY this fiscal year, with no major production capacity bottlenecks since the business does not require large-scale capital investment. CFO Hirooka: Optical Solutions Q1 sales grew 22%, or 11% at constant currency
quarterly_data.figure: CUPO sales growth approximately 30-40% YoY expected; Optical Solutions sales +22%

quarterly_data.signal: CFO Hirooka: Life Care Q1 revenue was 154.8 billion yen, up 13% (3% at constant currency), with operating profit of 29.9 billion yen (+24%) and a 19.4% margin (slightly below 19% excluding U.S. tariff refunds), progressing toward a target margin of around 20%; eyeglass lens sales grew 16% with the second-generation MiYOSMART iQ expanding in China; the Endoscope business continues structural reforms, and HOYA has initiated a review of strategic options including a possible transfer of the Endoscope business to a third party
quarterly_data.figure: Life Care revenue 154.8 billion yen (+13%); operating profit 29.9 billion yen; margin 19.4%

quarterly_data.signal: CFO Hirooka: the company expects conditions in each business to remain broadly similar to Q1, but the first-half outlook factors in the headwind from Q1's one-time U.S. tariff refund profit
